q: Terras (1976) and others studied the distribution of the stopping time σ(n) = min{k : Syr^k(n) < n}. For most n, σ(n) behaves statistically like:
opts: σ(n) ≈ log n / log(4/3) (approximately geometric in log n)
exp: Heuristically, each step of Syr multiplies by 3/2^{ν} where ν is geometric(1/2), giving average factor 3/4 per step. The stopping time σ(n) ≈ log(n) / log(4/3) ≈ 2.4 log₂(n) steps on average. Empirically σ(n) = O(log n) for all n tested.
